title: A traveller describes Gupta society
body: The Chinese traveller Faxian visited India in the early 5th century CE to see sacred Buddhist sites, learn from Indian scholars and collect Buddhist manuscripts. In his travelogue he wrote that the people of the Gangetic plains were numerous and happy, that those who farmed royal land paid a portion of their grain, and that the king's guards and attendants received salaries. He described rich, prosperous cities where heads of Vaishya families set up houses for charity and medicines, and where the poor, orphans and the sick received food and treatment. Elsewhere in the same travelogue, however, Faxian describes the harsh treatment of the chandalas, who were regarded as outcastes and had to live outside the city limits.
